objective: Among daily environmental clusters in metropolitan São Paulo, did the high temperature-variation/low-humidity/high-pollution cluster have higher daily acute myocardial infarction admissions or in-hospital mortality than the low-temperature-variation/intermediate-humidity/low-pollution reference cluster?

scientific_invariants.research_question: Among daily environmental clusters in metropolitan São Paulo, did the high temperature-variation/low-humidity/high-pollution cluster have higher daily acute myocardial infarction admissions or in-hospital mortality than the low-temperature-variation/intermediate-humidity/low-pollution reference cluster?
scientific_invariants.target_outcome_and_population: Daily acute myocardial infarction admissions and in-hospital deaths among SUS-hospital patients in 39 municipalities of metropolitan São Paulo.
scientific_invariants.principal_contrast: High temperature-variation/low-humidity/high-pollution environmental cluster versus low temperature-variation/intermediate-humidity/low-pollution cluster.
principal_variants: Daily AMI admissions across all three hierarchical environmental clusters
Daily in-hospital AMI mortality across all three hierarchical environmental clusters
scientific_invariants.broad_geography: 39 municipalities in metropolitan São Paulo, Brazil

article_evidence.finding: Supplied PubMed record identifies outcome/population, pollutant-weather feature set, source names, and compares admissions/mortality across hierarchical clusters.
ScienceDirect public Methods snippet establishes October 2012 through September 2015, correcting the broader contract period.

article_evidence_map.discrepancy_with_study_target: Article evidence specifies Oct 2012–Sep 2015; contract says Jan 2012–Dec 2015. Article-derived period controls.
article_evidence_map.full_text_status: Supplied PDF is an abstract record; ScienceDirect landing page inspected but full article body route blocked.

execution_design.exposure_metric: daily tmax, tmin, temperature variation, precipitation and relative humidity; explicitly no pollutant metric

coverage_policy.evidence: complete 1095-day weather series; pollutant coverage was 0% from tested public routes

execution_design.intended_use: bounded proxy sensitivity only, not the article-aligned pollutant analysis

amendments.scientific_justification: Feasibility probes found no usable OpenAQ historical PM2.5 record, and the article-named CETESB historical export is account-gated. A weather-only proxy sensitivity is retained separately while preserving the pollutant-cluster target as unrecovered.
